key: Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvastar’s Bull, Here in the mansion of the Moon.
s: In a hymn to Indra, the verse follows the tale of Dadhyac’s bones and the horse’s head; Sāyaṇa, on 1.84.15, reads it as the sun’s rays recognising in the Moon’s clear watery orb their own light, hidden by night.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.84.15, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400850 (2024)

evidence.words: अत्राह अस्मिन्नेव "गोः गन्तुः "चन्द्रमसो "गृहे मण्डले “त्वष्टुः दीप्तस्यादित्यस्य संबन्धि "अपीच्यं रात्रावन्तर्हितं स्वकीयं यत् "नाम तेजः तदादित्यस्य रश्मयः "इत्था इत्थमनेन प्रकारेण “अमन्वत अजानन् । उदकमये स्वच्छे चन्द्रबिम्बे सूर्यकिरणाः प्रतिफलन्ति ।
evidence.gloss: Right here, in the house, that is the orb, of the moving (go) moon, the rays of the sun knew thus, in this manner, the name, that is the light, belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ, the shining Āditya: their own light, which is hidden at night. The sun’s rays are reflected in the moon’s clear, watery orb.

reason: Both problems hold. (1) ‘the verse turns to the Moon’ was the batch formula: now ‘the verse follows the tale of Dadhyac’s bones and the horse’s head’, which day.js bears out (1.84.13 Dadhyac’s bones, 1.84.14 the horse’s head at Saryanavan, 1.84.15 the key). (2) ‘know their own light ... as reflected in’ was hard to parse and weakened his verb: Sāyaṇa glosses amanvata as ajānan and places the knowing ‘in the house, that is the orb’ of the moon (gṛhe maṇḍale), with the rays’ own light hidden at night (rātrāv antarhitaṃ svakīyam), then says the sun’s rays are reflected in the clear watery lunar orb (udakamaye svacche candrabimbe). Now ‘reads it as the sun’s rays recognising in the Moon’s clear watery orb their own light, hidden by night’, every part in the evidence, re-opened in packet.js veda 10 --verse 1.84.15; Wilson’s note agrees. 39 words. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.84.15, at [83,15]); entry-check ok.
